question: A newly diagnosed smear-positive pulmonary TB patient has CBNAAT confirming drug-sensitive TB (DS-TB). Under the current NTEP regimen, what is the correct treatment?

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Correct. The current NTEP DS-TB regimen is 2 months of HRZE (intensive phase) followed by 4 months of HRE (continuation phase), all given as daily weight-based FDC tablets. The old intermittent (thrice-weekly) regimen has been retired.
Incorrect. The thrice-weekly intermittent regimen has been retired by NTEP and replaced with daily FDC therapy. Citing the intermittent regimen is a major clinical error in current practice.
Incorrect. Ethambutol (E) is part of both the intensive phase regimen. The standard NTEP intensive phase is 2HRZE, not 2HRZ.

answers.text: 6HRE (six months of isoniazid, rifampicin, and ethambutol throughout).

tipsAndFeedback.chosenFeedback: Incorrect. The standard DS-TB regimen is 2HRZE + 4HRE, not a flat 6-month three-drug regimen. Pyrazinamide is essential in the intensive phase for sterilising activity.

overallFeedback.feedback: Revisit the NTEP DS-TB regimen section. The current regimen is 2HRZE (intensive) + 4HRE (continuation) — all daily FDC. The intermittent thrice-weekly regimen has been officially retired.
Correct. 2HRZE + 4HRE as daily weight-based FDC is the NTEP DS-TB standard. Never cite the retired intermittent regimen.
